title: Protocol for detection of ferroptosis in cultured cells
protocol: Determine the volume of growth medium required to seed the 384-well plate.
Collect cells from a T-75 flask into a 15 mL conical tube.
Determine the concentration of cells using a manual or automatic cell counter.
Use growth medium to dilute an appropriate volume of harvested cells to a concentration of 1,500 cells per 20 μL in a sterile trough.
Seed 20 μL of the cell solution per well of a black, clear bottom 384-well plate.
Spin the plate for 3 s at 58 × g to ensure cells adhere to the bottom of the wells.
Place the plate in a sterile 37°C CO2 tissue culture incubator for 16–32 h.
Treat cells with cell death inducers and inhibitors on day 2.
Prepare the cell death inducers by determining the volumes of growth medium and cell death inducer required to prepare a solution three times more concentrated than the desired highest dose.
Determine which cell death inducer requires the largest volume of stock solution and add an equivalent volume of DMSO for the 3× DMSO solution.
Prepare the 3× solutions of each cell death inducer in 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Add 50 μL of growth medium to columns 3‒11 and 14‒22 of a 384-well storage plate using a multichannel pipette.
Pipette 100 μL of each 3× cell death inducer solution into the appropriate wells in columns 2 and 13.
Add 50 μL of the 3× cell death inducer solution from column 2 to column 3 to achieve a two-fold dilution using a multichannel pipette.
Mix up and down six times to mix.
Repeat the previous step until you have reached column 11, which will result in a 10-dose serial dilution.
Repeat steps with new pipette tips for columns 13‒22.
Add 40 μL of the 3× DMSO solution to the appropriate wells in columns 12 and 23.
Determine volumes of growth medium and cell death inhibitor required for a three times more concentrated solution than the desired final concentration.
Calculate the total volume of growth medium needed as (number of cell death inducers × 11 wells) × (20 μL per well) + overage.

For each cell death inhibitor, calculate the volume of stock solution needed using the formula: (desired final concentration × 3) × (total volume calculated in previous step) ÷ concentration of stock solution.
Identify which cell death inhibitor requires the largest volume of stock solution and add an equivalent volume of DMSO for a 3× DMSO solution.
If measuring cell death via STACK, prepare a 60 nM SYTOX Green solution using growth medium (three times the desired final concentration of 20 nM).
In small sterile troughs, prepare the three times concentrated solutions of each cell death inhibitor.
Using a multichannel pipette, add 20 μL of each cell death inhibitor solution to the appropriate wells of the assay plate.
Pipette 20 μL of the cell death inducer solutions from the storage plate to the appropriate wells of the assay plate.
If using both STACK and CellTiter-Glo, add 60 μL 20 nM (1×) SYTOX Green solution per well to three wells without cells.
If using only CellTiter-Glo, add 60 μL growth medium (without SYTOX Green).
To make a 1× SYTOX Green solution, combine 100 μL 60 nM (3×) SYTOX Green solution with 200 μL growth medium.
Spin the assay plate down for 3 s at 58 × g.
Place the assay plate in a sterile 37°C CO2 tissue culture incubator for 48 h.
Set the red channel acquisition time to 800 ms.
Set the green channel acquisition time to 400 ms.
Set the spectral unmixing parameter to 8% of red contributes to green, 0% of green contributes to red.
Measure cell viability and/or death on Day 4+.
Use the 2D CellTiter-Glo assay to measure cell viability upon completion of the treatment if relevant.
Thaw the CellTiter-Glo Luminescent Cell Viability Assay reagent at 4°C the day prior to use.
Warm the plate and CellTiter-Glo reagent to approximately 21°C, 30 min before the treatment is complete.
If performing STACK in addition to CellTiter-Glo, do not remove the plate from the imaging machine until the final scan has been completed.
Remove 35 μL from each well of the 384-well assay plate.
Add 25 μL CellTiter-Glo reagent to each well.
Place the plate on an orbital shaker for 2 min.
Incubate the plate at approximately 21°C for 10 min.
Record luminescence using a microplate reader.
Calculate the mean luminescence signal of the three blank wells.
Subtract the mean blank signal from the luminescence signals of each experimental well.
Calculate the mean luminescence signal of the control wells.
Divide the blank-corrected luminescence values of each well by the mean control signal to obtain the relative cell viability.
Generate dose-response curves for each cell death inducer by log10 transforming the cell death inducer concentrations.
Use GraphPad Prism software ‘log(inhibitor) vs. response – Variable slope (four parameters)’ analysis.
Calculate the nonlinear regression best-fit curve.
Analyze STACK results if relevant.
Launch the image analysis using parameters described in the materials and equipment section.
Copy and paste the mKate2+, SYTOX Green+, and Yellow+ (red and green overlap) object counts per mm² into a spreadsheet.

Determine the lethal fraction for each condition by calculating 1 minus the ratio of mKate2+ minus Yellow to the sum of mKate2+ minus Yellow plus the maximum SYTOX Green+ count observed between times t = 0 and t = n, where n is the elapsed time in one time course experiment.
Confirm that cell death quantifications match the observed cell phenotypes by examining images such as Figure 3C.
Look for any potential issues by reviewing the data and images.
Generate dose-response curves for each cell death inducer by log10 transforming the concentrations.
Use GraphPad Prism software ‘log(inhibitor) vs. response – Variable slope (four parameters)’ analysis to calculate nonlinear regression best-fit curve.
Generate time-course graphs for each cell death inducer at a chosen concentration.
Plot time on the X-axis and lethal fraction on the Y-axis.
Use GraphPad Prism software ‘Plateau followed by one phase association’ analysis to calculate the best-fit curve.
Note that the calculated X0 value represents the death onset.
Design your plate layout.
Determine the volume of growth medium required to seed the plate.
Harvest cells from a T-75 flask and obtain cell counts using a manual or automatic cell counter.
Use growth medium to dilute an appropriate volume of harvested cells to a concentration of 2,500 cells per 20 μL in a sterile trough.
Seed 20 μL of the cell solution into the appropriate wells of a 384-well ultra-low attachment U-bottom assay plate using a multichannel pipette.
Spin the plate down at 350 × g for 5 min.
Place the plate in a sterile 37°C CO2 tissue culture incubator for 16–32 h.
Check cells under the microscope to ensure spheroid formation.
Treat cells with cell death inducers and inhibitors as described in the previous section for 2D cell culture.
Add 20 μL of 3× cell death inhibitors to the assay plate.
Add 20 μL of 3× cell death inducers prepared in 3× SYTOX Green medium to the assay plate.
Omit SYTOX Green if live cell imaging will not be used to assess cell death.
If using 3D CellTiter-Glo for assessing cell viability, add 60 μL of 20 nM (1×) SYTOX Green solution per well in three wells without cells.
Place the assay plate into the Sartorius S3 Live Cell Analysis Instrument or similar imager housed within a tissue culture incubator if monitoring cell death by live cell imaging.
Otherwise, place the assay plate carefully into a sterile 37°C CO2 tissue culture incubator for 48 h.
Set the red channel acquisition time to 800 ms for live cell imaging.
Set the green channel acquisition time to 400 ms for live cell imaging.
Set the spectral unmixing parameter to 12% of red contributes to green and 0% of green contributes to red for live cell imaging.
Thaw an aliquot of CellTiter-Glo 3D Cell Viability Assay reagent at 4°C the day before measuring cell viability.
Measure cell viability using the CellTiter-Glo 3D Cell Viability Assay.
Warm both the 3D CellTiter-Glo reagent and the plate to approximately 21°C.
Remove 30 μL from each well of the 384-well assay plate, including the three blank, cell-free wells.
Thoroughly mix the 3D CellTiter-Glo reagent by inversion.
Add 30 μL of the 3D CellTiter-Glo reagent to each well of the assay plate, including the three blank wells.
Cover the plate with foil and shake on an orbital shaker for 5 min to lyse the cells.
Incubate the plate on a benchtop at approximately 21°C for 25 min.
Record luminescence using a microplate reader.
Determine the optimal dose and treatment duration for each cell death inducer before conducting validation experiments.
Plot the dose-response data at 48 h using GraphPad Prism for each cell death inducer.
Fit a nonlinear regression curve to the plotted dose-response data.
Compute EC50 and Hill slope values from the fitted curve.
Determine the EC90 dose based on the computed values.
Plot kinetic data near the EC90 for one or more concentrations.
Generate a model fit using the ‘Plateau followed by one-phase association’ model in GraphPad Prism.
Extract the X0 value, which represents death onset from the model fit.
Select a time point approximately 30 minutes before death onset for each cell death inducer.
Seed 150,000 cells in 2 mL growth medium per well of a 6-well plate.
Seed enough wells to account for all conditions.
Include two wells for each apoptosis inducer: one for the inducer alone, and one for co-treatment with a pan-caspase inhibitor.
Include one well for treatment with the pan-caspase inhibitor alone.
Repeat experiments where cleaved caspase-3 is detected in wells treated with cell death inducers previously unknown to induce apoptosis.
Allow cells to adhere and proliferate for 2 days total (including the cell death inducer treatment).
Treat cells with each cell death inducer for a period equal to the death onset minus 30 minutes (see Table 4 for death onset values).
Aspirate medium from each well and replace with 2 mL of the appropriate cell death inducer (and, if applicable, inhibitor) solution.
Stagger treatments such that all end 48 hours after cell seeding.
Place plate on ice when treatments are complete.
Remove growth medium from each well.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold PBS to each well.
Remove the PBS and add another 1 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Scrape cells into PBS with a cell scraper.
Collect cell solutions into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Prepare RIPA buffer with protein and phosphatase inhibitors during centrifugation.
Remove PBS from the cell pellets.
Resuspend cell pellets in 100 μL RIPA cocktail.
Sonicate samples at 60% amplitude (1 s on, 1 s off) for 10 cycles.
Centrifuge samples at maximum speed for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to new Eppendorf tubes.
Quantify protein concentration using a BCA assay.
Prepare samples containing 25 μg protein each.
Add 4× Bolt loading dye and 10× reducing agent to achieve final concentrations of 1×.
Boil the samples for 5 min at 95°C.
Load 80% of the sample (20 μg protein) into a polyacrylamide gel.
Run the gel at 100 V for 1 h 45 min.
Transfer proteins from the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane using the iBlot 2 Gel Transfer Device.
Probe the membrane in a hybridization bag with rabbit anti-cleaved caspase-3 antibody and mouse anti-tubulin antibody diluted in Intercept Blocking Buffer at 1:1,000 and 1:2,000 respectively.
Incubate the membrane at 4°C on an orbital shaker for 16–32 h.
Wash the membrane three times (5 min each) with 1× TBST.
Dilute donkey anti-rabbit IgG antibody and donkey anti-mouse IgG antibody at a ratio of 1:15,000 in Intercept Blocking Buffer.
Incubate the mixture at approximately 21°C for 1 hour on an orbital shaker in a hybridization box.
Wash the membrane three times (5 minutes each) at approximately 21°C with 1× TBST.
Rinse the membrane once quickly with deionized water.
Store the membrane in deionized water until imaging.
Image the membrane using a LI-COR imager in both 700 nm and 800 nm channels to detect cleaved caspase-3 and tubulin signals.
Export the images for each channel in black and white.
Use an image analysis software to measure the cleaved caspase-3 signals for each condition.
Normalize these values to the respective tubulin signals by division.
Seed 50,000 cells in 1 mL growth medium per well of a 12-well plate.
Aspirate medium from each well.
Replace with 1 mL of the appropriate cell death inducer (and, if applicable, inhibitor) solution.
Prepare C11-BODIPY(581/591) and Hoechst solution in PBS 30 min before treatments are complete.
Add C11-BODIPY(581/591) for a final concentration of 1.5 μM.
Add Hoechst for a final concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Remove the growth medium from the wells approximately 15 min before treatments end.
Add 500 μL of the C11-BODIPY(581/591) and Hoechst solution to each well.
Incubate the plate in a sterile 37°C incubator for 10 min.
Remove the C11-BODIPY(581/591) and Hoechst solution from the wells.
Add 500 μL pre-warmed PBS to each well.
Image cells on a Lionheart instrument or similar imager using Texas Red, DAPI, and GFP filter cubes.
Calculate the C11-BODIPY(581/591) oxidation ratio for each condition.
